drop_off_rule: Show items published within the last 7 days. Remove any item more than 14 days after its date_published, even if fewer than 10 items remain.

items.title: Apple opens Siri AI to every app through App Intents in the iOS 27.3 developer preview
items.summary: Starting with the iOS, iPadOS, macOS and visionOS 27.3 betas, any app can expose its content and actions to Siri AI via App Intents, including personal context, onscreen awareness and new multi-step skills, with App Store submissions opening in the spring.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Customers with iOS apps can now make them agent-callable from Siri, so start mapping their key actions to App Intents and skills in the beta before the spring submission window, keeping in mind it's unavailable in the EU for now.

items.title: Anthropic open-sources FlashProve, a prototype that cryptographically proves which model produced a reply
items.summary: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team released FlashProve under Apache 2.0: a provider commits to hidden model weights, then generates a zero-knowledge proof per reply that anyone can verify on a CPU, demonstrated on Llama 4 Maverick at about 110 tokens per second on one H100.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: It's a research prototype with no deployment plans, but it points to a future where customers can audit that a vendor really served the model they pay for, so don't promise it today and do watch it for regulated deals.

items.title: OpenAI quadruples bug bounty rewards, with critical ChatGPT, Codex or API findings now paying up to $30,000
items.summary: OpenAI raised its security bug bounty ranges, added quality, loyalty and priority-campaign multipliers that can lift exceptional findings to about $172,000, and will apply the new ranges retroactively to recent reports.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: If your team finds a flaw in ChatGPT, Codex or the API while building for a customer, report it through the program rather than working around it quietly, since the payout and disclosure path are now worth it.

items.title: GitHub Actions will block pull_request_target by default in public repos starting December 2
items.summary: GitHub pushed enforcement back a month to December 2, 2026, with brownouts before then, and the rule already runs in evaluate mode so you can see which workflow runs it would block unless an Actions event policy explicitly allows the trigger.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Any customer repo whose CI, AI review bot or agent workflow uses pull_request_target will break on December 2, so audit those workflows now and either move them to pull_request or add an explicit allow policy.

items.title: Anthropic's amended S-1 says it uses Claude to help build the next Claude and flags recursive self-improvement as a safety risk
items.summary: The S-1/A filed on Nov 2 says internal Claude usage is accelerating Anthropic's development, warns that using AI to build more capable AI could pose a considerable safety risk, and says its Responsible Scaling Policy covers the approach to what has been termed recursive self-improvement.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Expect customers to ask about this after the headlines; the filing itself is a risk disclosure, not a claim that self-improving AI has arrived, so point them to the exact language.

items.title: OpenAI is merging ChatGPT's Chat and Work tabs, and ChatGPT and Codex will share one usage allowance
items.summary: According to an email OpenAI sent users, the merged experience starts with select users before a wider rollout, Codex stays a separate section of the desktop app, and ChatGPT and Codex will draw from the same token allowance pool.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Teams that lean on Codex heavily may hit usage resets sooner once the pools merge, so recheck seat and plan sizing for customers running both.

items.title: Mistral releases open weights for Mistral Large 4, a 1T-parameter model aimed at cybersecurity and coding agents
items.summary: Mistral Large 4 is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model with about 1T total and 49B active parameters and a 1M-token context, released in FP8 and NVFP4 under Mistral's open-weight license, with day-one support in Transformers, vLLM and llama.cpp.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: A frontier-class model customers can self-host for security work that closed APIs often refuse, but check the license's limits on model-as-a-service before building a hosted offering on it.

items.title: Researchers show a single ChatGPT share link could take over a signed-in user's account; OpenAI has fixed it
items.summary: Parameter Labs chained a graph library's virtual keyboard, an unguarded postMessage handler and a YouTube endpoint allowed by ChatGPT's content security policy to run their own JavaScript as chatgpt.com, read private chats and exfiltrate them, and OpenAI patched it on Oct 26 as a P1.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: If you ship sandboxed AI-generated HTML or artifact previews for customers, audit every postMessage listener and every domain your CSP allows, because one permissive allowance broke this sandbox.

items.title: Google DeepMind announces Gemini 4 Carbon, its new frontier model, with a limited rollout to cyber defenders first
items.summary: Google says Gemini 4 Carbon is its strongest model for long-horizon coding, agentic and cybersecurity work, priced at $2 in and $10 out per million tokens, but for now only a subset of cyber defenders get access while broader developer availability waits on more guardrail work.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Plan for it but don't promise it to customers yet: there's no general API access date, so keep current Gemini 4 Argon or other deployments in place and prep evals for when Carbon opens up.

items.title: GitHub Copilot Fusion is generally available, routing each task across multiple models
items.summary: Instead of picking one model, Copilot Fusion decides which models to use per prompt, and GitHub says its Max level scored within two points of Claude Code with Opus 5.5 Max at about half the cost per task.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: A cheaper default for customers on Copilot, but routing makes behavior less predictable, so pin a specific model where reproducible output matters.

items.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows is generally available
items.summary: GitHub's open source Agentic Workflows lets teams describe tasks like issue triage, CI failure analysis and test writing in Markdown, which compile into standard GitHub Actions run by Copilot or another coding agent.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: A supported way to put coding agents into a customer's existing Actions runners and policies, instead of standing up a separate agent platform their security team has to approve.

items.title: OpenAI will honor a shared robots.txt signal for AI training opt-outs
items.summary: OpenAI says it will respect a common robots.txt signal that lets website operators tell participating AI providers whether their content may be used for training.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Customers who publish content now have one standard place to state training preferences, so add it to the web-governance checklist when they ask how to control AI crawling.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Terra, a fast midrange model for computer use and agentic coding
items.summary: GPT-6.1 Terra is a cheaper, faster tier below GPT-6.1 Sol that OpenAI pitches for visual reasoning, computer use and clearer writing, and it is already live in GitHub Copilot and Vercel AI Gateway.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: A cheaper midrange option for repetitive computer-use and form-filling agents; rerun your evals before switching customer workloads off Sol.

items.title: GitHub Enterprise now includes Copilot, metered against the enterprise AI budget
items.summary: Enterprises working with a GitHub or Microsoft account team can get Copilot for every GitHub Enterprise user, with AI usage billed from the first request against the enterprise budget instead of per-seat credits.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: For GitHub Enterprise customers, Copilot cost becomes a usage-budget conversation, so set budgets and alerts up front because chat, code review and cloud agent stop when the budget runs out.

items.title: Anthropic launches reporting tools that show enterprises what their Claude spend is producing
items.summary: Anthropic introduced analytics that let managers see a team's work over a date range, what it produced, what it cost and where workflows stall.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Gives you built-in ROI reporting for Claude rollouts, which is usually the question a customer's budget owner asks at renewal.
